text.p: Latvia's leading commercial bank Pareks Bank said on Wednesday that it was considering a listing of its shares on the stock exchange.

"The shareholders have such ideas (on a bourse listing) because we have a lot of lucrative proposals involving private placements," Pareks vice-president Viktor Krasovitsky told Reuters at a conference on investing in the Baltics here.
"The logic of our development is pushing us in that direction," he added.
Krasovitsky said the example of Estonia's Hansapank, the largest bank in the Baltics and quoted on the Tallinn bourse, was "inspiring".
Pareks had earlier it was not considering a bourse listing as it did not want to share its profits without outside shareholders.
Unibanka is so far the only bank to have listed its shares on the bourse.
